name: Benin
regionLevel: first-level division (ISO 3166-2), as in the N-Ways regions table

existing.system: No national postcode system. La Poste du Bénin addresses use P.O. boxes: in Cotonou, Porto-Novo, Abomey and Parakou a two-digit delivery-office prefix precedes the box (e.g. '10 BP 648, COTONOU'). Cotonou has a municipal street-numbering plan (Cellule municipale d'adressage, launched 2013; streets coded by arrondissement, e.g. 'Rue 12.048'), but signage is sparse.
existing.status: Re-checked 2026-10-12: still no live address or postcode system. On 22 April 2026 the Council of Ministers authorised a national strategy for standardising street and door addressing ('nouveau système d'adressage innovant et participatif, numérique et géolocalisé'), first in Abomey-Calavi, Cotonou, Ouidah, Porto-Novo, Sèmè-Podji and Parakou, through a specialised consultancy; no ministry, timeline, format, platform, tender or progress report has been published since. Plan only.
existing.openData: None usable: no open street-address dataset from any official programme. OpenStreetMap (ODbL) holds 946 house numbers in the whole country.
existing.terms: No licence published for any official address dataset.
existing.recommendation: The N-Ways code (docs/model.md: plate name + number, unique nationally) is the shareable address of every compound, shown beside any official address; spot codes and N-Ways' landmark descriptions for any other point; 'BP' boxes kept as free text. No postcode is invented. The addresses of the 2026 national strategy are shown first once delivered.

sources.note: AFP 2018: Cotonou numbers generally not displayed

findings.name: Cotonou Cellule municipale d'adressage (PA2D, French cooperation, 2013; 'Plan d'adressage de Cotonou' map 2015)
findings.state: legacy, dormant (signs and numbers generally not displayed, AFP 2018; no update found 2022–2026)
findings.format: streets coded by arrondissement ('Rue 12.048'), door numbers roughly metres along the street, odd/even sides

findings.name: 'Adressage participatif' demonstrator (adressage.up.railway.app, Algorithme)
findings.state: unofficial demo ('aucun caractère officiel'), counters at 0
findings.format: proposed street names for the six pilot communes
findings.openData: says 'open' but no licence; dossier by email only

findings.name: ANDF cadastre / e-Foncier (cadastre.bj, cadastre.andf.bj)
findings.state: live (≈460,000 parcels in Feb 2023, mostly Cotonou)
findings.format: land title number, lot, quartier: parcel references, not addresses
findings.openData: no download, API or reuse licence found

findings.name: ANIP / ASIN / Bénin Révélé
findings.state: no digital-address product found (ANIP e-services issue a residence certificate only)

findings.name: Open data portals (data.gouv.bj, HDX)
findings.state: road datasets only (CENATEL 2006; World Bank AICD 2009, CC-BY 4.0; OSM extracts, ODbL)

osm.note: Far too sparse for house-level geocoding; the 55 addr:postcode tags can't be real postcodes. No official address import listed on the OSM wiki.

sources.buildings: OpenStreetMap (ODbL); Google Open Buildings (CC BY 4.0) and Microsoft building footprints (ODbL) via Overture Maps
